look: XORA site look, same as the V00 welcome film: deep void ground, frosted glass panels with thin cyan-to-violet edges, fictional market lines drawing in, calm eased motion, the brain tutor guiding from the bottom-right corner

scenes.name: Lesson eighteen
scenes.desc: Title card: Phase 4, lesson T18, volume, volatility and range; volume bars rise under candles; the tutor walks in.

scenes.name: Same change, different ride
scenes.desc: Two fictional charts both go from 60,000 to 60,100: one calm, one jumpy.

scenes.name: Volume
scenes.desc: Volume defined; a shop counting sales; trades of 2, 5, 3 and 2 BTC fill a 12 BTC volume bar, about 720,000 USDT.

scenes.name: Volume bars
scenes.desc: Fifteen fictional candles with a volume bar under each; quiet and busy minutes.

scenes.name: Range
scenes.desc: Range is high minus low: 60,300 − 60,000 = 300 USDT, 0.5% of the low.

scenes.name: Volatility
scenes.desc: Calm lake vs choppy sea: quiet candles average a 40 USDT range, volatile ones 250 USDT.

scenes.name: Previous high and low
scenes.desc: A 10-minute lookback window gives 300 USDT (0.5%); stretched to 15 minutes, 600 USDT (1%).

scenes.name: Two windows compared
scenes.desc: Window A: 150 USDT range (0.25%), low volume, fees take a big share. Window B: 900 USDT (1.5%), high volume, bigger swings.

scenes.name: Liquidity context
scenes.desc: A 2 BTC market buy in a busy book fills at 60,000; in a thin book it averages 60,050: 50 USDT per BTC of slippage.

scenes.name: Common mistake
scenes.desc: A huge volume bar is not proof of buyers: 40 BTC bought means 40 BTC sold.

scenes.name: Know the limits
scenes.desc: Past ranges promise nothing, volatility can jump, leverage and slippage, WAIT allowed.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Three key points and one question to check yourself.

scenes.name: Up next
scenes.desc: End card: next lesson T19, what is scalping (Phase 5).
